<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
 I've got enough context now to move forward. I'll add a new prompt to the chezmoi config for installing IAC tools, then create an ansible role to handle the actual installation with the necessary tasks.

I need to register this role in both the macOS and Linux playbooks with the `iac_tools` tag, update the ansible runner script to include the role hash and conditionally apply the tag, and modify the Dockerfile to accept the install flag. I'll also need to update the documentation—adding the new tag to CLAUDE.md, creating a dedicated tools guide, and updating the README's tools section.

For the actual installations, I'm planning to use Homebrew on macOS for Azure CLI, and on Linux I'll use the official Microsoft installation script with sudo, falling back to pip for non-root environments.

Terraform will use Homebrew on macOS and HashiCorp's apt repository on Linux (with sudo), while non-root installs can grab the precompiled binaries directly. OpenTofu follows a similar pattern with Homebrew on macOS and their deb repository or standalone installer on Linux, with GitHub releases as the non-root fallback.

Since both Terraform and OpenTofu are just single static binaries, this is pretty lightweight overall. I'm thinking one unified `installIacTools` prompt makes sense rather than separate toggles for each tool, and I'll include all three since the user indicated they're not heavy and didn't exclude any of them.

Let me check the README to see if there's a tools list that needs updating.</details></think>

  "plan": "## Scope\n\nInstall three Infrastructure-as-Code CLIs behind a single &#96;installIacTools&#96; chezmoi prompt (default &#96;false&#96;):\n\n- **Azure CLI** (&#96;az&#96;) — per [Microsoft's install doc](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/install-azure-cli)\n- **Terraform** (&#96;terraform&#96;) — HashiCorp\n- **OpenTofu** (&#96;tofu&#96;) — Linux Foundation fork\n\nTerraform and OpenTofu coexist (different binary names), so installing both is zero-conflict. All three are lightweight CLIs (Terraform/OpenTofu are single static Go binaries; Azure CLI is a Python bundle but ships as an OS package).\n\n## Install matrix\n\n- macOS (Homebrew, always): &#96;brew install azure-cli terraform opentofu&#96; — Terraform requires the &#96;hashicorp/tap&#96;; OpenTofu is a first-class formula (&#96;tofu&#96;). Pattern mirrors the speedtest tap handling in [dot_ansible/roles/networking_tools/tasks/main.yml](dot_ansible/roles/networking_tools/tasks/main.yml) lines 25–40.\n- Linux with sudo (Debian/Ubuntu):\n  - Azure CLI: Microsoft apt repo (keyring + source list + &#96;apt install azure-cli&#96;).\n  - Terraform: HashiCorp apt repo (keyring + source list + &#96;apt install terraform&#96;).\n  - OpenTofu: official install script &#96;get.opentofu.org/install-opentofu.sh --install-method deb&#96; (adds repo + installs &#96;tofu&#96;).\n- Linux noRoot (&#96;[sudo]&#96; tag skipped):\n  - Terraform \u0026 OpenTofu: download architecture-matched zip from GitHub releases → extract single binary to &#96;~/.local/bin/&#96; (same pattern as other &#96;~/.local/bin&#96; installs in the networking role).\n  - Azure CLI: &#96;uv tool install azure-cli&#96; (consistent with existing &#96;python_uv_tools&#96; role). Gated behind &#96;uv&#96; being present; warn-and-skip otherwise.\n- Architecture guard: install only on &#96;x86_64&#96;/&#96;aarch64&#96; (wrap in a &#96;when:&#96; check + &#96;rescue&#96; block, matching the networking role's robustness pattern).\n\n## Files to create\n\n- &#96;dot_ansible/roles/iac_tools/tasks/main.yml&#96; — install tasks (macOS homebrew block, Linux sudo apt block, Linux noRoot user-level block). Follow the &#96;rescue:&#96; + &#96;failed_when: false&#96; pattern from [dot_ansible/roles/networking_tools/tasks/main.yml](dot_ansible/roles/networking_tools/tasks/main.yml).\n- &#96;dot_ansible/roles/iac_tools/defaults/main.yml&#96; The slow install times for Azure CLI and Terraform suggest the user's connection to GitHub Container Registry is either unstable or geographically constrained, possibly due to network restrictions in China. The OpenTofu failure is a direct result of this—the download was interrupted mid-transfer.

I should check whether OpenTofu actually installed despite the failure, then offer practical solutions like retrying the installation manually, configuring a Homebrew mirror through environment variables, or switching to a direct binary installation from GitHub releases. The core problem is that the Homebrew Ansible module lacks built-in retry logic, so when curl times out, the task fails immediately without recovery attempts.

I can fix this by adding retry logic to the Ansible tasks—using `retries` and `until` conditions to automatically retry failed Homebrew installs a few times with delays between attempts. I should also add rescue blocks for graceful degradation, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the playbook for handling network failures on Linux.
